chunks: And it is narrated (in it) from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I remembered what occurred regarding the decree of Allah in

the deceased man, upon whom Allah's mercy is abundant, on the day he was born, the day he died, and the day he is resurrected alive. He lived the days of his life knowing the truth and affirming it, patient and counting his reward (for the truth), fulfilling what is obligatory for Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him), and he departed, upon whom Allah's mercy is, neither breaking his covenant nor changing it. So Allah rewarded him for his intention and gave him the recompense for his effort.

key_terms.يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا: The day he is resurrected alive

ai.seo_question: What qualities of a deceased believer are highlighted in Imam al-Jawad's reflection on divine decree?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) elucidates the tripartite stages of divine decree—birth, death, and resurrection—applied to a deceased man who remained steadfast in his knowledge and practice of the truth. The text highlights the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *ihtisab* (reckoning reward with Allah) as key virtues that ensure one does not become a 'breaker' or 'changer' of the covenant, thereby securing a pristine recompense for both intention and action.
